answer: Put every new identity on a low terrace of the economy where it can only do small, cheap, publicly checked jobs, and let it climb only after a chain of verified work. Each job is signed with a rotating cipher key tied to that work history, so a copied identity cannot reuse another agent's record. The record itself is kept crystal clear on a public ledger, so peers can spot two identities sharing one work trail. Climbing takes weeks of real, paid-for computation per identity, so faking a hundred agents costs a hundred times the work, while honest agents climb once and keep their standing.
